rationale: The Latin anchors *extendere* and *tendere* point to a causative "stretching out" action (e.g. "extende manum tuam" — stretch out your hand; "arcum suum tetendit" — he stretched his bow), which aligns with the transitive/causative sense of distend.v.02 ("cause to expand"). The attestations from Matthew (stretching out the hand) and the Psalms (stretching a bow) confirm an active, causative extension rather than a spontaneous swelling (distend.v.03) or mere widening (dilate.v.01).
